artifacts.summary: Grounds the dispatch's live-host-measured Sapience scoping/noise-gate findings in the actual codebase call sites (memory-retrieve.sh, orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh Stage 3.5) and the vendor mcp.py source's exact auth mechanism and /ingest-kos KO shape; flags a direct conflict with subagent-orientation.md's existing anti-goal language.

memory_candidates.content: Sapience's vendor MCP client (~/.sapience/mcp.py) authenticates every HTTP call -- GET /v1/search and POST /ingest-kos alike -- via a token=<TOKEN> query-string parameter appended to the URL (see api() helper), not an Authorization: Bearer header. Token precedence: SAPIENCE_TOKEN env var, else ~/.sapience/config.json's "token" field. Host likewise: SAPIENCE_HOST env var, else config.json's "host", else https://app.spnc.ai default.

Sapience's POST /ingest-kos body shape (confirmed from mcp.py's sapience_remember tool): {"token": ..., "kos": [{"subject", "predicate", "object_value", "ko_type", "confidence", "provenance", "explicit"?, "source_loc"?}], "source": "<tag>"}. A caller's repo-tag and explicit:true flag both belong inside the single KO object in kos[0], not as top-level body fields.

An extension manifest's provides.scripts list (e.g. agent-system/extensions/memory/manifest.json) names scripts under that extension's own scripts/ subdirectory that sync-manifest-scripts.sh deploys to .claude/scripts/. A new script referenced by a deployed-path call site (e.g. orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh invoking "${SKILL_REPO_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/...") will not actually exist post-deploy unless its owning extension's manifest.json declares it in provides.scripts -- adding the file alone, without the manifest entry, is a silent no-op after redeploy.
